model.name: Emails as scenario units
model.description: Each email is an ior:class:Email scenario unit linked to its profile via the class-to-method relationship pattern; a profile may carry multiple emails, which act as alternate lookup keys with the same device-link behavior as phones.
model.tronQuote: > TRON: "ior:class:Email linked to profile via relationships (like class to method). Multiple emails per profile. Same alternate-UUID + device-link behavior as phone."
model.architectureRef: ior:file:scrum.pmo/sprints/sprint-21-contact-identity/architecture.md#1-object-graph + #2-alternate-uuid-index + #3-device-link-on-known-key (Email unit shape, alt/email symlink, resolveKeyToProfile shared with R21.4)

acceptanceCriteria.text: Each email is minted as an ior:class:Email scenario unit with its own v4 uuid in scenario/index.
The Email unit model carries { uuid, address (normalized), ownerIor } — the address field stores the NORMALIZED form.
ownerIor points to the owning Profile (nav parent, NOT a chain edge); the Profile carries the forward IOR in model.emails[].
Profile.model.emails[] holds the forward IOR(s) to Email unit(s) (class-to-method relationship shape).
A profile may carry MULTIPLE Email units, each an independent ior:class:Email with its own uuid.
Idempotent: linking an email whose normalized address already exists on the profile creates NO duplicate Email unit and NO duplicate entry in emails[].
normalizeEmail is deterministic and pure; the SAME implementation is shared by server and client.
The normalized form is what is stored as the unit address AND used as the alt-index key (one canonical value).

The alt/email/<normalizedAddress>.scenario.json symlink is declared on the PROFILE unit unitLinks[] (matches shipped R21.6 phone) and points to the Profile unit; index.put self-syncs it (ensureSymlinkDisk), remove() self-removes it.
The alt/email entry resolves DIRECTLY to the owning Profile — making the email an alternate UUID for that profile (parallel to R21.3 phone).
resolveKeyToProfile(normalizedEmail) returns the owning Profile uuid (read the symlinked Profile unit model.uuid), or null on miss.

EmailIndex.mintAndLink(profileUuid, rawEmail): normalize -> mint-or-reuse the Email unit (ownerIor=Profile) -> push its IOR into Profile.emails[] -> add alt/email link to Profile.unitLinks[] -> index.put.
EmailIndex.mintAndLink is idempotent: calling it twice with the same email on the same profile yields exactly ONE Email unit and ONE emails[] entry and ONE alt/email symlink.
EmailIndex.mintAndLink returns the Email unit IOR.
On IDENTIFY with an email already in the alt/email index, resolveKeyToProfile returns the existing profile and the device-link flow (R21.4) runs — NO new user is minted.
Email device-link is IDENTICAL to phone (R21.4): correct secret code -> a new device attaches to the existing profile; wrong/absent code -> no device, no profile merge.

testScenarios.name: normalizeEmail trim+lowercase
testScenarios.then: returns "marcel.donges@gmail.com"; pure (repeat calls identical); this value is both the stored address and the alt key

testScenarios.name: Email unit shape + owner
testScenarios.given: a profile with uuid P and raw email a@B.de
testScenarios.then: an ior:class:Email unit exists with model {uuid, address:"a@b.de", ownerIor:P}; P.model.emails[] contains the Email IOR

testScenarios.name: mintAndLink wires Profile.emails[]
testScenarios.then: Email unit minted (ownerIor=P), P.emails[] gains its IOR, Profile.unitLinks[] gains alt/email/a@b.de..., and the call returns the Email IOR

testScenarios.name: multiple emails per profile
testScenarios.then: two distinct ior:class:Email units exist, both IORs in P.emails[]

testScenarios.name: idempotent re-link
testScenarios.when: mintAndLink(P,"A@B.de") is called again (normalizes to same key)
testScenarios.then: still exactly ONE Email unit, ONE emails[] entry, ONE alt/email symlink — no duplicate

testScenarios.name: alt symlink on Profile.unitLinks (code is law)
testScenarios.then: P.model.unitLinks[] contains "alt/email/a@b.de.scenario.json" and the on-disk symlink resolves to P scenario file (NOT to the Email unit)

testScenarios.name: resolve email -> profile
testScenarios.given: profile P linked to "a@b.de" and an unknown "x@y.de"

testScenarios.name: email device-link on known key
testScenarios.given: profile P (secretCode S) with email "a@b.de" in the index; a new device connects with email "a@b.de"
testScenarios.when: IDENTIFY resolves the email -> P, prompts for code, device sends the code
testScenarios.then: correct code S -> new device attached to P (no new user); wrong code -> DEVICE_ENROLL_FAILED, no device, no merge — identical to phone (R21.4)
